category_title: Adolescent with emotional/behavioral disorder and academic frustration
minimal_context: Isaac is sitting at his desk during class time to complete an independent math quiz on a tablet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Isaac, it is time for your independent math assignment. Please log into the tablet and complete the quiz questions.

STUDENT: This is a waste of time. I'm not doing these stupid math problems.

TUTOR: You need to finish the assignment. Just do your best.

STUDENT: I can't do it! I don't know these facts! (Scribbles aggressively all over his assignment paper)

TUTOR: Keep trying, Isaac. Look at the next question on the tablet.

STUDENT: I said I'm not doing it! (Grabs the tablet and throws it onto the floor, breaking it, then tears a page out of his math book)

options.A: Prompt Isaac to obtain his math materials if he had not already done so at the beginning of class.
options.B: Practice using math flash cards with corrective feedback and a number line to illustrate the math facts.
options.C: Agree with Isaac that he is having a rough time with the independent math quiz in this session.
options.D: Withhold all attention from Isaac regarding his disruptive behavior during the independent math assignment in this session.
